$comment: COPY → ~/.paseo-pi-team/model-routing.local.json on EACH host. Never commit the local copy: it holds host-specific model choices. Values below are placeholders — run 'paseo provider ls' and 'paseo provider models <role-provider> --json' on the host, then fill in real IDs. 'paseoProvider' names the runtime family AND the role: pi-<role> or claude-<role>. The model reference shape follows the family: pi = '<pi-provider>/<model-id>' (the model id may itself contain slashes, e.g. 'openrouter/vendor/model-name' — Paseo splits at the FIRST slash only); claude = a bare model id such as 'claude-opus-5'. 'thinking' is family-specific too: pi ∈ off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max, claude ∈ off|low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultracode, and it must be supported by the model (check model.thinkingOptions; for custom pi models in ~/.pi/agent/models.json, a thinkingLevelMap entry of null means the level is silently clamped by pi — treat it as unsupported). Routes may mix families freely: one class on pi, another on Claude, on the same host.
